summary:
ASTRA

ASTRA is a student-built prototype designed to support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions. Our prototype includes NFC-based identification and session access, a physical touchscreen interface, and a computer-vision module that tracks facial landmarks, expression-related movements, and head orientation.

ASTRA addresses the challenge by establishing a foundation for personalized health check-ins and understandable monitoring. NASA research on fatigue, isolation, and communication delays informs our design, emphasizing the need for useful onboard support when immediate assistance from Earth is limited.

Our future vision combines available facial, voice, sleep, and activity information across sessions to investigate earlier warnings of specific concerns. The proposed assistant would explain observations, request clarification when information is uncertain, and support appropriate human review. Predictive monitoring and fully local operation remain future developments requiring testing and scientific validation.

ASTRA aims to help astronauts recognize meaningful changes and communicate concerns clearly, while maintaining a clear distinction between observed indicators and medical conclusions.
details:
What exactly does it do?

ASTRA helps astronauts check their physical and mental health during a mission. It tracks mood, symptoms, sleep, reaction time, breathing and exercise. It alerts the Flight Surgeon when something looks wrong, and it raises an SOS with an alarm in emergencies. It has an AI assistant called Astra that answers health questions by text or voice.

How does it work?

The astronaut signs in by tapping an NFC crew card. They do quick check-ins on the touchscreen: mood, symptoms, a reaction test, a breathing exercise, or SOS. Tapping an NFC tag on an object, like the treadmill or a food packet, logs it automatically. Everything shows up live in the web app: health trends, sleep, mood, a 3D body model, real NASA missions, and a 3D astronaut coach that shows how to do each exercise. The Flight Surgeon sees the whole crew and gets the alerts.

What benefits does it have?

Astronauts can follow their own health without waiting for Earth. Problems like stress, poor sleep or missed exercise are caught early. In an emergency, help is called right away.

What do you hope to achieve?

We want to replace our demo data with real NASA health data. We also want to add vibration alerts for when the sound or headphones fail. Our goal is a reliable health companion for long missions like Mars.

Tools & Technologies

Languages: Python, JavaScript, Arduino (C++)

Backend: Flask, Socket.IO

Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS

3D: Three.js, React Three Fiber, NASA 3D Resources models

AI model: GPT-OSS 120B through Groq (Astra chatbot)

Voice: Microsoft Edge text-to-speech, browser speech recognition

Face ID: face-api.js

Hardware: ESP32 CYD touchscreen, Raspberry Pi Pico with a PN532 NFC module V3, NFC cards and tags

Version control: Git, GitHub
